main_text.p: illum propter se conditam esse agnoscat: deniq; ita revereatur virum suum, quemadmodum lunam videmus revereri solem, in cujus præsentia splendorem suum plurimum contrahit. In absentia viri potestas domus sit penes uxoré, sic tamen ut nihil contra voluntatem illius tentet: in præsentia vero abstineat ab imperio, claudat os, & aperiat aures ad audiendum mariti sui vocem: hujus imperium agnoscat, obediat, & sponte quidem: imò & amet eundem candidè, verè & sinceriter. Arduum enim id est, quod sanctissimum Christi & Ecclesiæ exemplum proponitur, quo non sanctius aliud invenias. Necesse ergo est sanctum quoque sit matrimonium, & amor ejus eximius.

Omnia autem eloquitur Apostolus propriissimis verbis. Uxores, inquit, τοῖς ἰδίοις viris subditæ sitis. Propriis, inquit, significanter. Per hoc enim illud obsequium excludit, quod scortū scortatori, & adultera adultero præstat. Samaritana illa mulier, de qua Joan. 4. quinque viros habuit, sed non suos, i. proprios. Notatur ergo his verbis fides matrimonii, & excluditur scortationis vanitas atque perfidia. Deinde addit, Veluti Domino: non quia sit æqualis authoritas, sed quia mulieres Christo obedire neque unt[?], nisi se obsequentes viris præbendo: &, ne qua arrogantius obijceret: Egon' subderer illi viro? Ideo, Subditæ sitis, ait scientes, quòd serviatis Deo: hoc est, si non propter virum: inpri-

page.notes: Right edge carries fragments of the neighbouring page and is omitted. Left margin marks are show-through and omitted. Greek "τοῖς ἰδίοις" is transcribed from a superscript-style setting; its accents are uncertain at the scan resolution. "neque unt" is doubtful (possibly "neque sunt") and is marked [?]. "propriissimis" is read from a slightly blurred "priifsimis" and the printed hyphen after "pro-" is taken from the line end. Long s has been rendered as plain s throughout, including where the scan shows f-like forms (solem, suum, esse). The final line "inpri-" is a line-end hyphenation; "mis" below is the catchword.
